_schema.purpose: Plain-language translation layer for healer alerts. Render-time lookup keyed by (source, subject); on match, surface severity + summary + recommended_action above a collapsed technical-detail footer. See docs/runbooks/add-new-healer-alert.md.
_schema.lookup_rule: Exact match on subject first; if miss, strip trailing ':'-segments from subject one at a time and retry. First match wins (longest-prefix). Source must match exactly.
_schema.severity_note: Display-only label, decoupled from the producer's queue severity ('warning' | 'critical'). URGENT does NOT imply queue severity='critical' — it's the operator-facing urgency.
_schema.tier_note: Operator-triage gradient (spec: agents/beacon/specs/operator-ux-alert-taxonomy.md). NOW = blocks the chain right now, requires immediate action. SOON = needs attention within hours. FYI = informational, no action required. Conservative classification — when uncertain, lean toward FYI rather than NOW. Unknown subjects (not in this table) default to SOON in the renderer per spec § 2.
_schema.stopgap_note: Translation layer is a stopgap until the Pulse cycle upgrade (follow-up to PR #108) ships healer-alert triage as a core Pulse responsibility. Once Pulse triages, this table can retire; the CI gate that enforces every healer has an entry stays useful as an ergonomics review trigger.

pipeline-stall:forge-no-pr.plain_language_summary: Forge finished a build but the PR never opened. The branch was pushed (or at least built) but `gh pr create` failed silently — the chain stalled because Mirror has nothing to review.
pipeline-stall:forge-no-pr.recommended_action: Check ~/agent-worktrees/wt-forge-<task_id>/ for the branch state and ~/agents/logs/inbox_watcher.log around the alert timestamp for the gh error. If the branch is pushed, run `gh pr create` manually from the worktree. Runbook: runbooks/heal-pipeline-stall.md.

pipeline-stall:marker-invisible.plain_language_summary: Mirror finished a review but the outbox-notifier never parsed her marker — the verdict block was wrapper-shaped or inline-prefix shaped instead of canonical `=== REVIEW_PASS ===` / `=== REVIEW_REVISION ===`. The chain stalled because the verdict is invisible to the dispatcher.
pipeline-stall:marker-invisible.recommended_action: Open the Mirror session for the named task and re-emit the verdict via `scripts/marker.py render mirror <type>`. Don't hand-type marker blocks. Runbook: runbooks/heal-pipeline-stall.md (marker-invisible section).

pipeline-stall:no-session-revision.plain_language_summary: A REVIEW_REVISION verdict dispatched a revision back to Forge but didn't carry a `--resume <session_id>` — Forge will start fresh with no context from the original build session, which usually means re-solving the same problem.
pipeline-stall:no-session-revision.recommended_action: Check the notifier session at ~/agents/logs/outbox_notifier.log around the alert timestamp for the missing session_id. Re-dispatch the revision with the original session_id pulled from inbox-watcher's session log, or accept the cold-start cost. Runbook: runbooks/heal-pipeline-stall.md.

pipeline-stall:retry-exhausted.plain_language_summary: The MAX_RETRIES loop in agent_runner.py burned through every attempt for this task without success. The chain stopped because retrying further would just hit the same wall — likely a stuck premise, missing dependency, or upstream blocker.
pipeline-stall:retry-exhausted.recommended_action: Read ~/agents/logs/<agent>.log filtered to the named task_id to find the recurring failure mode. Either fix the upstream issue and re-dispatch, or REJECT the task from the inbox with a reason. Runbook: runbooks/heal-pipeline-stall.md.

pipeline-stall:tier2-fallback-failed-rat.plain_language_summary: Tier 1 (agent Claude Max account) hit a rate-limit AND the Tier 2 fallback (HOME-swap to /home/larry/.claude-larry-personal) also failed. Both accounts are limited or one of them has stale credentials.
pipeline-stall:tier2-fallback-failed-rat.recommended_action: Wait for Tier 1's reset window (the original CLI error gives the time). If Tier 2 should have worked, audit credentials per docs/runbooks/restore-larry-personal-claude-oauth-tier2.md. The chain is paused on this task; it will not auto-recover.

pipeline-stall:tier2-fallback-unavailabl.plain_language_summary: Tier 1 OAuth hit a 401 (expired refresh token) AND the Tier 2 fallback directory at /home/larry/.claude-larry-personal is missing or unprovisioned. The chain is stuck — no working account to retry against.
pipeline-stall:tier2-fallback-unavailabl.recommended_action: Run `python3 scripts/auth_orchestrator.py` to re-authenticate Tier 1, OR `python3 scripts/auth_orchestrator_tier2.py` to provision Tier 2. Full recovery steps: docs/runbooks/restore-larry-personal-claude-oauth-tier2.md.

install-drift.plain_language_summary: A systemd unit is shipped in the repo's `systemd/` directory but is NOT installed at /etc/systemd/system/. The unit isn't running on this droplet — whatever the unit does (a daemon, a timer, a healer) is silently absent.
install-drift.recommended_action: Run `sudo cp systemd/<unit-name> /etc/systemd/system/ && sudo systemctl daemon-reload && sudo systemctl enable --now <unit-name>` from the repo root. Verify with `systemctl status <unit-name>`. Runbook: runbooks/heal-systemd-install-drift.md.

stuck-timer.plain_language_summary: A relative (monotonic) systemd timer lost its next-fire anchor — `NextElapseUSecMonotonic` went to `infinity`, meaning it would never fire again — and the healer auto-recovered it with a daemon-reload + restart. This typically happens when a daemon-reload catches an `OnUnitActiveSec` timer mid-cycle. Self-healed; no action needed unless the same timer trips repeatedly.
stuck-timer.recommended_action: None required — already auto-healed and re-armed. If a specific timer trips this repeatedly, convert it from `OnUnitActiveSec` to `OnCalendar` in systemd/<name>.timer (absolute schedules populate `NextElapseUSecRealtime` and cannot lose their anchor). Verify: `systemctl show <unit> --property=NextElapseUSecRealtime`. Runbook: runbooks/heal-systemd-install-drift.md.

credential-drift:MISSING_REGISTRY_ENTRY.plain_language_summary: A credential exists on disk (e.g., a token file, OAuth refresh token, API key) but has no entry in config/token-rotation-schedule.json. It's invisible to rotation tracking — when it expires, it will silently die instead of being rotated on schedule.
credential-drift:MISSING_REGISTRY_ENTRY.recommended_action: Add an entry to config/token-rotation-schedule.json for the named credential per the existing entries' shape (4-artifact discipline: registry + runbook + calendar event + drift-healer awareness). Runbook: runbooks/heal-credential-registry-drift.md.

chain-event-shipper-stale.plain_language_summary: The chain-event-shipper daemon has not posted a heartbeat in over its threshold. Mission-control dashboard is now showing stale data — the chain may or may not be moving, but you can't see it from the UI.
chain-event-shipper-stale.recommended_action: Run `sudo systemctl restart chain-event-shipper.service` and check `journalctl -u chain-event-shipper.service -n 50` for the underlying error. If the shipper crashes immediately on restart, inspect ~/agents/logs/chain_event_shipper.log for the stack trace.

auto-merge-queue-corrupt.plain_language_summary: The auto-merge queue file at ~/agents/blackboard/auto-merge-queue.json failed to parse — JSON syntax error or structural surprise. The notifier has fail-closed: every subsequent auto-merge attempt is HELD until the file is repaired and the daemon restarts.
auto-merge-queue-corrupt.recommended_action: Inspect the file with `cat ~/agents/blackboard/auto-merge-queue.json` to find the corruption. Move it aside (`mv ... .broken`) to clear the queue, then `sudo systemctl restart outbox-notifier.service`. Recovery steps: runbooks/auto-merge-queue.md.

bots:pulse:tmux.plain_language_summary: Pulse-bot is running via tmux (the intended deployment after PR #161). No action needed unless the tmux session is also down.
bots:pulse:tmux.recommended_action: If you want to verify or relaunch: `tmux has-session -t pulse-bot` to check, `bash ~/agent-core/scripts/pulse_telegram_bot.sh` to (re)launch into the same tmux session. Do NOT run `sudo systemctl restart ourliberty-pulse-bot.service` — that would start a second pulse-bot instance competing with tmux for getUpdates.

bots:pulse:down.plain_language_summary: Pulse-bot is DOWN: both the tmux session and the systemd unit failed liveness checks. No Telegram pulse-side traffic is flowing.
bots:pulse:down.recommended_action: Relaunch the intended tmux deployment: `bash ~/agent-core/scripts/pulse_telegram_bot.sh`. Verify with `tmux has-session -t pulse-bot && tmux capture-pane -p -t pulse-bot | tail -20`. Runbook: runbooks/watchdog-bot-policy.md.

bots:beacon:down.plain_language_summary: Beacon-bot is DOWN and the auto-restart carve-out also failed. Telegram alert delivery itself is broken — DMs cannot reach you until beacon-bot is back.
bots:beacon:down.recommended_action: Run `sudo systemctl status ourliberty-beacon-bot.service && sudo journalctl -u ourliberty-beacon-bot.service -n 50` to find the failure mode, then `sudo systemctl restart ourliberty-beacon-bot.service`. Runbook: runbooks/watchdog-bot-policy.md.

bots:forge:down.plain_language_summary: Forge-bot is DOWN and systemd has not recovered it — StartLimitBurst (10 starts / 300s) likely exhausted. Forge tasks queued in the inbox will not be picked up.
bots:forge:down.recommended_action: Run `sudo systemctl status ourliberty-forge-bot.service && sudo systemctl restart ourliberty-forge-bot.service`. Check `journalctl -u ourliberty-forge-bot.service -n 50` for the underlying crash cause. Runbook: runbooks/watchdog-bot-policy.md.

bots:mirror:down.plain_language_summary: Mirror-bot is DOWN and systemd has not recovered it — StartLimitBurst likely exhausted. PR reviews queued for mirror will not run.
bots:mirror:down.recommended_action: Run `sudo systemctl status ourliberty-mirror-bot.service && sudo systemctl restart ourliberty-mirror-bot.service`. Check `journalctl -u ourliberty-mirror-bot.service -n 50` for the underlying crash cause. Runbook: runbooks/watchdog-bot-policy.md.

claude_tier1_failed_on_resume_session_bo.plain_language_summary: A Beacon chat turn failed mid-session and could not auto-retry on the backup (Tier 2) account, because Claude session IDs are tied to one account. Beacon itself stays running — only that one turn failed. Most often the underlying cause is a brief Anthropic server-side throttle (HTTP 429, 'not your usage limit') that clears on its own, NOT a real quota or auth problem.
claude_tier1_failed_on_resume_session_bo.recommended_action: First just send a fresh Beacon message — it starts a new (non-resumed) session and routes normally, which usually confirms recovery on its own. Only if the fresh message ALSO fails, probe `claude -p --output-format json 'say ok'` under each tier HOME (Tier 1: /home/larry; Tier 2: /home/larry/.claude-larry-personal) to tell apart a real auth-401 (re-login needed) from a usage-cap (wait for the rolling-5h window). NOTE: the raw alert's 'wait for the 5h window' advice is often wrong — the classifier currently mislabels transient 429s as auth_401 (fix queued).

claude_max_5h_burn_threshold_breached.plain_language_summary: The trailing-5h Tier 1 quota-consuming token volume (input + output + cache_creation, from costs.jsonl; cache_read excluded) crossed 80% of the configured pace gate (tier1_quota.max_5h_token_threshold). This is a leading proxy for the real rolling-5h Anthropic rate-limit window — heads-up that sustained pace will hit the wall if it continues. No money is involved (OAuth Max has no per-token billing); the prior dollar framing was retired 2026-05-28.
claude_max_5h_burn_threshold_breached.recommended_action: Decide whether to pause dispatches or let the rolling-5h window cycle out. For ground-truth quota state, check https://console.anthropic.com/settings/usage; for the actual rate-limit-event log, see ~/agents/blackboard/anthropic-quota-events.jsonl. The threshold is auto-tuned weekly by scripts/pulse_check_viii.py against precision/recall on the event ledger — don't hand-tune.

tier2_weekly_probe_failed.plain_language_summary: The backup (Tier 2) OAuth account failed its weekly health probe — the automatic failover safety net may be down. The primary (Tier 1) account is unaffected, but if Tier 1 ever hits its limit there would be no working fallback.
tier2_weekly_probe_failed.recommended_action: Re-auth Tier 2 per docs/runbooks/restore-larry-personal-claude-oauth-tier2.md. Manual re-probe: `HOME=/home/larry/.claude-larry-personal claude -p --model claude-opus-4-7 'say ok'` — a clean 'ok' means Tier 2 is healthy again.

sync-blocked.plain_language_summary: ourliberty-sync refused to fast-forward main from origin. The working tree on the VM is not receiving PR merges until the underlying block is cleared.
sync-blocked.recommended_action: ssh ourliberty-vm, `cd ~/agent-core && git status` to see the gating condition. Most common causes: uncommitted modifications, wrong branch checkout, divergence with origin. Resolve per the more-specific subject (uncommitted-changes / wrong-branch / fast-forward-failed).

sync-blocked:uncommitted-changes.plain_language_summary: ourliberty-sync refused to pull because ~/agent-core has uncommitted modifications. Commonly Pulse runtime files (cycle-journal, cycle-actions, MEMORY) left dirty by an interactive /cycle — those should now auto-commit; anything else is human-touched dirt.
sync-blocked:uncommitted-changes.recommended_action: ssh ourliberty-vm, `cd ~/agent-core && git status` to identify the dirty files. If they are Pulse-owned, commit + push manually; otherwise commit/stash the human work. Sync resumes on the next tick once the tree is clean.

sync-blocked:wrong-branch.plain_language_summary: ourliberty-sync refused to pull because ~/agent-core is checked out on a non-main branch. Per the ourliberty-agent-core operating model, all work commits direct to main; a feature branch on the VM is unexpected.
sync-blocked:wrong-branch.recommended_action: ssh ourliberty-vm, `cd ~/agent-core`, `git checkout main`, and merge or discard the feature branch as appropriate. Then sync will resume on the next tick.

sync-blocked:fast-forward-failed.plain_language_summary: ourliberty-sync tried to fast-forward main from origin/main and failed — the local repo and origin have diverged. The chain stops receiving PR merges until the divergence is resolved.
sync-blocked:fast-forward-failed.recommended_action: ssh ourliberty-vm, `cd ~/agent-core`, run `git log --oneline origin/main..HEAD` to see what is local-only, then rebase or hard-reset to origin/main once it is safe to drop the local commits.

sync-blocked:validation-failed.plain_language_summary: ourliberty-sync pulled a new commit from origin/main but validate_agent_core.py rejected it; the sync rolled back to the previous HEAD. The tree is consistent but stuck behind origin until the bad commit is fixed upstream.
sync-blocked:validation-failed.recommended_action: ssh ourliberty-vm, `cd ~/agent-core`, `git checkout <new-head>`, then `python3 scripts/validate_agent_core.py` to see what failed. Fix on origin/main; the next sync tick will pick it up.

sync-blocked:quiescence-timeout.plain_language_summary: ourliberty-sync ran with REQUIRE_QUIESCENCE=1 and the strict-quiescence wait exceeded its timeout; sync rolled back. A non-quiescent agent kept the tree from being safely swapped.
sync-blocked:quiescence-timeout.recommended_action: ssh ourliberty-vm, `cd ~/agent-core && python3 scripts/await_quiescence.py` to identify the busy agent(s). Resolve before the next sync tick (or let sync run without REQUIRE_QUIESCENCE if soft-quiescence is acceptable).

cycle-tier-corrupted.plain_language_summary: The cycle-tier state file was missing or had an invalid schema, so the system reset it to the Tier 1 defaults and kept running. Nothing is stuck, but a recurrence means something keeps corrupting that file.
cycle-tier-corrupted.recommended_action: One-off: no action needed, it self-recovered. If it recurs, inspect ~/agents/state/cycle-tier.json by hand for what is writing bad data.

check-iv-update.plain_language_summary: The weekly marker-drift check found Mirror's marker shape is drifting often enough to propose tightening enforcement (prompt re-emphasis or a hard validator gate). This is a proposal awaiting your call, not a failure.
check-iv-update.recommended_action: Review the proposal and reply `approve check-iv-update-<date>` or `reject check-iv-update-<date> <reason>` on Telegram. No action keeps the current enforcement unchanged.

check-v-update.plain_language_summary: The Tier-1 action-template trust check proposes changes to the guard list: graduating templates that have earned trust, or adding ones that triggered a correction. This is a proposal awaiting your call, not a failure.
check-v-update.recommended_action: Review the proposals and reply `approve check-v-update-<date>` or `reject check-v-update-<date> <reason>` on Telegram. No action leaves the guard list as-is.

check-vi-update.plain_language_summary: The PRIME DIRECTIVE posture check proposes tuning the verification-pending handling (auto-promote window or stuck-forever thresholds) based on the last 30 days. This is a proposal awaiting your call, not a failure.
check-vi-update.recommended_action: Review the proposals and reply `approve check-vi-update-<date>` or `reject check-vi-update-<date> <reason>` on Telegram. No action leaves the current posture unchanged.

check-vii-update.plain_language_summary: The cost-ceiling check proposes tuning the spend-escalation thresholds based on recent escalation-response history. This is a proposal awaiting your call, not a failure.
check-vii-update.recommended_action: Review the proposals and reply `approve check-vii-update-<date>` or `reject check-vii-update-<date> <reason>` on Telegram. No action leaves the current thresholds unchanged.

rotation_auth_gate_blocked.plain_language_summary: The scheduler tried to rotate the active Claude account into the next tier but that tier's OAuth credentials are missing, expired, or unverifiable, so it held on the current tier. The chain still moves on the held tier; it will retry the flip after you re-auth.
rotation_auth_gate_blocked.recommended_action: Re-auth the blocked tier so the next rotation window can flip. Runbook: docs/runbooks/restore-larry-personal-claude-oauth-tier2.md.

check-viii-update.plain_language_summary: The marker precision/recall floor check proposes raising, lowering, or deprecating a validation threshold based on the last week. A deprecate proposal is the strongest variant. This is a proposal awaiting your call, not a failure.
check-viii-update.recommended_action: Review the proposal and reply `approve check-viii-update-<date>` or `reject check-viii-update-<date> <reason>` on Telegram. No action leaves the current floors unchanged.

check-viii-defer.plain_language_summary: The marker precision/recall floor check could not auto-propose because both precision and recall fell below their floors this week, so it needs you to read the artifact and decide whether to raise, lower, or hold.
check-viii-defer.recommended_action: Read the week's artifact and decide manually whether to raise, lower, or hold the floors. No automated proposal applies here.

check-x-regression.plain_language_summary: The weekly chain-quality watch found that since the last model/prompt cutover, the Forge/Mirror build chain has gotten measurably harder on at least one quality signal (Forge needs more clarification rounds per task, or more build/revision rounds per task). This is CORRELATIONAL — the cutover happens to coincide with the rise; it is not proven cause. It is a heads-up awaiting your call, not an automated change.
check-x-regression.recommended_action: Review the recent Forge/Mirror PRs from the trailing window (the DM names the metric and shows the before -> after numbers). If the regression looks real, revert the affected agent to claude-opus-4-7 by flipping its routing value in config/agent-models.json and restarting the inbox-watcher (it caches config at startup, inbox_watcher.py:778). No automated action is taken; the full metric table is in ~/agents/blackboard/pulse-check-x-proposals/check-x-<Monday>.json.
